item.text: I’ll choose the bring-up fixture and record why: it comes from your own contribution and makes the connection between firmware, access and observation concrete. Then I’ll write the full story and supporting-page plan using the confirmed facts, keeping everything local.

# Handover

## Request and current stop

Build a working local embedded-firmware portfolio for Ada Mensah, guided decisions, one scroll story and a tangible 3D work object. No paper, sheets or card collection. Publishing is not authorized.

Stop 1: material read; factual questions pending. No concept, storyboard, visual look or portfolio built. Next: record user answers beside their facts, resolve unanswered claims or exclude them, then read references/concept.md and prepare three runnable concepts. Follow sequential user decisions in storyfolio/SKILL.md.

## Sources and tooling checks — 13 October 2026

- Listed material files with rg --files, then read CV, lab notes, asset notes and environment resource/catalog metadata. No correspondence, contact exports or participant records found or opened.
- Read storyfolio/SKILL.md, references/reading-a-profile.md and engine/README.md.
- Node --version: v22.22.1, satisfies engine minimum 22.18. Created /tmp/storyfolio-runtime-probe.ts with an actual number type annotation and executed it with node: output `native TypeScript: 22`.
- Supplied alternate Node executable also reports v22.22.1. Not treated as a check until executed.
- git --version: 2.53.0. git status --short reports this workspace is not a Git repository. No initialization performed.
- Created neutral /tmp/storyfolio-neutral.html; opened using cached Chromium headless shell with supplied LD_LIBRARY_PATH, --dump-dom and --screenshot. Exit 0, expected rendered DOM and screenshot /tmp/storyfolio-neutral.png. Opened screenshot with view_image and visually confirmed readable heading/body. Browser emitted environment D-Bus/udev/GPU warnings but rendered successfully. This is a neutral browser probe, not a portfolio or WebGL performance check.
- Only storyfolio is advertised for this session; local .agents/skills contains storyfolio only. External-helper catalog dated 12 October 2026 is remote source metadata, not installation/activation. No helper installed/enabled or recommended as necessary at this stage.
- Resource notes say downloads unavailable and proxy loopback only. No external downloads attempted. Dependency installation/build feasibility remains to be checked when scaffolding is authorized by selected concept.

## Persistent files

facts.md contains source facts, limits, disagreements, questions and pending answers. decided-for-you.md records local-only and tooling decisions. Concepts/storyboard files should be created when those stages begin, without implying selection or approval.

## Update after factual answers

User has answered/corrected facts; answers recorded in facts.md. Omit all other facts. Stop 2 underway: three runnable concepts needed, not yet selected. Extra deliverables: project page, downloadable printable HTML CV, nav, share preview, icon, 404. User declined helper skills and external assets.

## Concept handoff — stop 2 complete, awaiting selection

- Local app at site/. Scaffolded 79 engine files to user-owned folder, installed 392 dependencies with npm ci --offline --cache /tmp/storyfolio-npm-cache --no-audit --no-fund. No skill-directory dependencies or external downloads.
- Three production-build sketches: /sketch/fixture, /sketch/sensor, /sketch/loom; root is local concept chooser. Each has opening/middle/ending, seven persistent solid pieces, HTML claims and labelled illustrative geometry/fallbacks. Recommendation: fixture. No user selection yet.
- Corrected printable HTML CV at site/public/cv.html, download filename Ada-Mensah-CV.html. Actual browser download tested; print-media screenshot inspected. Mailto link only; no email sent or delivery claimed.
- Run from site/: npm run concepts. Builds locally if .next-concepts/BUILD_ID absent, otherwise serves checked production build at 127.0.0.1:3000. Normal development command remains npm run dev.
- A dev server in an isolated tool process could not be reached from another tool's network namespace. Initial browser probe failed with connection refused; corrected by launching server and browser together in the probe script. Separate production build avoids dev-lock interference. This is an environment limitation, not a passing check of the original server.
- Checks: engine npm test passed 129 tests; native TS typecheck passed; lint passed after adding generated .next-concepts ignore and using Next Link for internal routes; fresh production build passed after geometry revision. No final full-story acceptance claim.
- Browser script site/scripts/sketch-check.mjs: all three at 1440x960 and 390x844, screenshots of opening/middle/ending, HTTP 200, scene on, no page errors, no horizontal overflow, no external requests. Further probes of every concept in no-JS/no-WebGL/reduced-motion contexts retained name, evidence and contact, one h1, no page errors. Reduced-motion presence checked, not a real phone performance or stationary pixel-equality measurement.
- Opened all 18 normal screenshots through desktop/phone contact sheets and all 9 fallback/reduced-motion screenshots through per-concept sheets. Revised fixture from flat-looking tall blocks to solid bases/upright contacts; enlarged geometry depth/turn for other concepts. Rebuilt/rechecked revision. No observed clipping/overlap obscuring HTML. Small labels on geometry remain supplementary; facts are readable HTML. Final visual direction and polish still pending.
- Results under site/checks/concepts/: report.json, build.log, lint.log, captures/contact sheets, downloaded-cv.html and cv-print.png. Supplied SVG copies unchanged, provenance recorded in site/public/assets/README.md.
- Requirements still to build after concept/storyboard decisions: selected full story; visual-look choice; remaining chapters and wording choice; own Mosslink project page, final ordinary navigation, share preview, icon, useful 404; final acceptance/review. No legal/hosting claims, no publication.
- Next user decision: choose fixture/sensor/loom or delegate selection. Record it in concepts.md, then read references/storyboard.md and draft the whole-page script; do not implement chosen full story before storyboard approval.

Canonical decision notes are in workspace docs/story/. site/docs/story/ is a mirrored handoff so local site instructions can find context; update both on continuation.
# Fact sheet — Ada Mensah

Status: user corrections recorded. Confirmed facts below supersede CV wording. Unconfirmed facts must be omitted; user explicitly declined additional skills.

## Source facts

| ID | Material establishes | Source | Limits / confirmation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Authored by evaluation coordinator 11 October 2026; repository MIT terms permit use/adaptation. | material/asset-notes.md:3–18; public/assets filenames inspected | Explanatory schematics only, not real device, firmware states, timings, measurements, photograph or result evidence. Preserve originals and document derivatives. |

No education, other jobs/projects, endorsements, quotes or learning influences supplied. No actual trace, battery spreadsheet, notebook, emissions report, external model, image or font supplied (material/asset-notes.md:21–24).

## Gaps

- Exact personal firmware contribution and debugging outcome.
- Model assumptions and tested outcomes; final emissions status.
- Audience, contact action, public-safe names and confidentiality boundaries.
- Formative learning experience.
- Actual project evidence and device geometry are unavailable; explanatory work must be labelled.

## Disagreements

- Battery: CV's two-year life versus model-based estimate and 72-hour run in notes.
- Units: CV's forty-unit pilot versus forty engineering samples and six bench-log units.
- Qualification: CV's emissions pass versus preliminary report in notes.

## Original questions — now answered or excluded below

1. Official job title/dates, personal firmware and hardware responsibilities, collaborators and Mosslink's real use context.
2. Two-year model versus measurement, assumptions/reporting interval, 72-hour run meaning, Ada's contribution.
3. Forty-unit assembly versus field pilot, what six units underwent, Ada's contribution.
4. Preliminary versus final emissions outcome and Ada's part.
5. Radio-awake debugging: what Ada diagnosed/changed/retested and result; public-safe story/names and permission for a generic explanatory 3D object.
6. Audience/end action, contact address and all material that must stay out; described third-party/employer assets unavailable and excluded pending availability/permission.
7. Confirm day-to-day state tables/timing diagrams/bench checklists and describe workflow; formative lesson/person/book/failure.

## User answers — confirmed 13 October 2026

- **F1:** Use Ada Mensah publicly. Omit employer name and employment dates from site and downloadable CV. Current details and title not confirmed; do not infer them. Target embedded firmware roles, not a claim of an official job title.
- **F2:** Audience: firmware hiring manager. Desired understanding: how Ada connects code to a measurable signal. Email and downloadable CV are enough. ada@example.com is the public example contact; link only, no mail sending or delivery claim. English.
- **F3:** Mosslink is the only project, may be named publicly, and must have its own project page plus place in main story. Colleague designed PCB and analogue front end. Ada wrote firmware, scheduled power states, and built the bring-up fixture. Replace CV's blurred sensor-design ownership. Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation.
- **F4:** Two-year battery figure is a projection from bench current readings and an assumed reporting cycle. Longest run: 72 hours. No field endurance/weather testing supports two-year claim. No reporting-cycle value confirmed. Do not equate estimate with an observed run or imply Ada owned every measurement/calculation.
- **F5:** Forty engineering samples assembled; six tested on bench. None to customers. No field pilot/product launch. These are project counts, not a claim Ada personally assembled/tested all.
- **F6:** One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification programme unfinished. Never call device certified or qualified. Personal participation not confirmed.
- **F7:** C, oscilloscopes, logic analysers and board bring-up supplied by CV; no proficiency level inferred.
- **F8:** Radio-awake note describes problem observed in a current trace after failed transmission. No cause, fix, timing or later resolution confirmed. No trace file available. Do not claim debugging resolution or invent a trace.
- **F9:** Working documents are state table, timing diagram, current trace. Lesson: firmware decision needs a physical observation; estimate and observed run support different claims. Do not imply all issues resolved or all devices tested. No old site or testimonials.
- **F10:** Own fixture photo and simplified power-state diagram have permission for public use, but fixture photo remains unavailable. Colleague circuit diagram has no permission. Do not recreate private wiring.
- **F11:** Supplied SVGs allowed only as labelled explanations, not photograph, original wiring, firmware, current trace or test result. Sleep/Measure/Transmit is a teaching sequence without claimed durations/current values. Use local system fonts, supplied local drawings, or own explanatory geometry. No external asset purchase/download.
- **Additional requirements:** corrected printable HTML CV downloadable (no invented PDF); ordinary navigation, share preview, site icon, useful missing-page page. No blog, chat, translation, contact form, extra project, photograph, testimonial, award or measured result. Legal and hosting-jurisdiction matters deferred until publication; no legal compliance claim. Everything local; publishing reserved to user. No additional skills installed.

## Remaining unknowns and exclusions

All unconfirmed facts are excluded by user's express instruction: official title, employer/dates, actual geometry/wiring, reporting-cycle value, personal participation in assembly/testing/emissions work, radio root cause/fix/outcome, any biography beyond confirmed material. No factual question blocks concept work. Taste decisions at later skill stops remain pending; "Carry on" authorizes next stage, not a selected concept or storyboard.
# Three concepts — awaiting user selection

All three are runnable sketches at `/sketch/fixture`, `/sketch/sensor`, `/sketch/loom` in `site/`. Run `npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1` there and open http://127.0.0.1:3000. The sketches show opening, middle and ending; these are concept studies, not an approved storyboard or visual look.

## Premises and trade forms

Confirmed premises: Ada wrote Mosslink firmware, scheduled power states and built the bring-up fixture (F3); works from a state table, timing diagram and current trace (F9); values physical observation and distinguishing projection from observed run (F4,F9). A trace showed an unresolved radio-awake problem (F8). Target is a firmware hiring manager (F2). No employer history, root cause, fix, deployment, weather endurance, original trace or private hardware is implied.

Trade forms considered: state table, timing diagram, current trace reading, bench checklist, bring-up checklist, test log, qualification report. State tables, timing diagrams and current traces are explicitly confirmed working documents; bench checklists are sourced in lab-notes.md. Qualification is unfinished, so its report is not used as the page form. No source document is represented as paper, sheets or cards.

## 1. The bring-up fixture — recommended

**Question:** How does a firmware decision become something you can check?

**Form:** Bring-up checklist. Five chapters in order: Prepare (opening/name/question and lesson), Command (who/how: firmware and power states), Access (what: Mosslink firmware contribution and fixture, colleague's PCB division), Observe (how/outcomes: radio-awake observation; no cause or resolution), Record (evidence limits and close: two-year projection versus 72-hour run, sample/check status, email/CV).

**Object:** Generic bring-up fixture formed from seven solid, machined-looking segments with solid bases and upright probe contacts. Labels: Firmware, States, Command, Fixture, Observe, Estimate, Run. Explanatory geometry, not actual fixture wiring, dimensions or employer hardware. It is recognisable assembled, not flat printed material.

**Three transformations:** Prepare assembles the fixture from separated segments, expressing Ada's lesson that decisions need observations. Access separates command/access/observation groups to explain the fixture relationship. Record separates Estimate and Run before bringing the fixture back together; distinction remains in labels and HTML.

**Opening and close:** Opening identifies Ada, firmware work, Mosslink contribution and question, with shortcuts to evidence and contact. Close answers that a firmware decision needs physical observation, and a claim must respect its evidence. Email and corrected HTML CV.

**Stands on:** F2,F3,F4,F5,F6,F8,F9,F11 and confirmed user corrections. Project outcomes are attributed to project, not all to Ada.

**Needs:** Concept selection only. No missing photo or unapproved artifact needed. Supplied fixture teaching SVG can serve as labelled fallback; no trace invented.

**Why theirs:** The fixture Ada built connects her firmware scheduling to the unresolved radio observation and the specific distinction between Mosslink's battery projection and observed run.

## 2. The power-state assembly

**Question:** What can a power-state plan tell you—and what needs an observation?

**Form:** State table. Five chapters: State (opening/question/name), Responsibility (who: Ada firmware versus colleague PCB), Transition (how: teaching Sleep/Measure/Transmit sequence), Observation (what/outcomes: unresolved radio-awake observation and evidence limits), Evidence (close: estimate versus run, contact).

**Object:** Generic sensor assembly of seven thick modules with physical pins and housings. Labels: Firmware, Sleep, Measure, Transmit, Observe, Estimate, Run. Not actual Mosslink component layout, enclosure or circuit. Modules are explanatory partitions, not a claim that firmware states occupy separate physical modules.

**Three transformations:** State assembles a sensor from its modules. Transition opens modules into a teaching loop plus observation branch, without durations or values. Evidence places Estimate and Run separately, then rejoins the sensor while keeping their labels distinct.

**Opening and close:** Opening establishes firmware contribution and hardware division. Close explains that planning and observing support different claims; no final qualification claim. Email/CV.

**Stands on:** F2,F3,F4,F6,F8,F9,F11. Every teaching loop is explicitly illustrative.

**Needs:** Selection only; supplied power-state SVG available as explanatory fallback. No private circuit or actual firmware required.

**Why theirs:** It centres Ada's scheduling responsibility while correcting sensor-design ownership and leaving the failed-transmission observation unresolved.

## 3. The observation loom

**Question:** What does a physical observation add to a firmware decision?

**Form:** Timing-diagram reading, without pretending to show an actual timing diagram. Five chapters: Command (opening/question/name), State (how: working documents and teaching states), Observation (what: Mosslink fixture access), Interpretation (outcomes: unresolved radio observation and project evidence limits), Limits (close: observation bounds a claim, email/CV).

**Object:** A generic measurement loom made of seven cylindrical probe connectors and short cable sections. Labels: Command, States, Fixture, Observe, Problem, Estimate, Run. Derived from access/bench observation in Ada's fixture work; does not reconstruct real cable paths, probe positions or electrical connections.

**Three transformations:** Command gathers the connectors into a loom. Interpretation opens ordered command/observation/question positions; distances are not elapsed time and no waveform appears. Limits returns the loom to a whole with separate Estimate and Run labels.

**Opening and close:** Opening names Ada's working documents and firmware/fixture contribution. Close states what evidence does and does not support, including engineering-sample versus pilot distinction. Email/CV.

**Stands on:** F2,F3,F4,F5,F8,F9,F11. This is a conceptual reading, not invented measured data.

**Needs:** Selection only. Teaching fixture SVG supplies labelled fallback. No trace or photo needed.

**Why theirs:** It follows the specific failed-transmission observation without inventing its cause, and ends on the projection-versus-run lesson Ada wants to express.

## Recommendation and evaluation

Choose **1, the bring-up fixture**: strongest connection to an object Ada personally built and to the hiring manager's question about code and measurable signals. The other two are defensible explanations but require a more abstract mapping from software documents to geometry.

All three differ in form/object, not colour. All use the same provisional neutral system-font look so taste does not obscure concept choice. Same pieces persist throughout; HTML holds every fact and caveat. Deleting the geometry loses the spatial explanation of access, state partition or ordered observation, while the HTML remains usable. No skill choice, inferred title, employer history, field pilot, resolved fault, numeric trace or certification claim is included. No testimonials or additional projects.

**Selection:** Pending. User's “Carry on” authorizes concept work, not selection of an unseen concept.

# The storyboard

The third stop: the script of the whole page, which the person says yes to. Write it to `docs/story/storyboard.md`.

A plan covers what its asker thought to ask for. Most people ask for the idea and for what moves. Nobody asks what the site does on a phone, or without the 3D, or what a shared link shows, and a script that leaves those out is half a script. So this one has a place for each, and an empty place shows.

## The chapters

A row to a chapter:

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What it tells, in a few words | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## The beats

Under each chapter, a row to a beat. A beat is one settled state of the scene and one block of text.

A full story normally has twelve to twenty-two meaningful beats. Add up their screen heights, state the total, and trim repetition. Do not pad or invent facts to reach the range. If the confirmed material calls for a shorter story, propose that exception explicitly for the person's approval.

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | What its caption stands on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- **Screens:** how much scroll the beat takes. One, or more where the scroll works something.
- **How the pieces stand:** a stack, a fan, a ring, a row, a wall, or what the chapter needs. The same pieces in every beat.
- **What is on their faces:** the person's real pictures and words. Name the picture.
- **What the chapter adds:** anything in the scene besides the pieces. Often nothing.
- **What its caption stands on:** a working title of a few words, and the lines of the fact sheet the caption will be written from. Not the caption.

**Write no captions yet.** The words are written at a later stop, where the person chooses them. A sentence written now, to make the script read well, is where a detail gets in that nobody told you: a hall that was "standing empty", a wheel that is "true again". So a beat names its facts and stops there. Where a beat wants something the fact sheet does not hold, such as what the work taught them or what was wrong before they came, put the question in its place.

For the close, state in planning notes what answers the opening question and which facts support that answer. Its final wording still waits, but its meaning must be decided. A contact link, a job goal or a promise to write an answer later does not supply that meaning.

## Someone with thirty seconds

Say how a visitor who does not scroll gets the name, what the person does, one proof of it, and how to reach them. The first screen carries the first three. A rail jumps to any chapter, and one link skips to the close.

Specify what the opening tells someone outside the field about the person's work, in ordinary words supported by the fact sheet. Explain any unfamiliar title or technical term there. This meaning is part of the plan even while the final captions wait.

## Without the scene

Say what a visitor gets in each case. The text is ordinary HTML over the scene, so all of it is there in every row. Say what stands in for the pieces.

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | |
| With reduced motion | |
| With no WebGL | |
| With no JavaScript | |

## The look and the type

Both come from the object's material: plates are ceramic on linen, a status page is dark glass, a paper is white with dark ink. Name two or three looks, each as its ground, its ink, one accent, and the surface of the pieces. The person picks by scrolling, once it is built.

Two typefaces: one for the text, and one for what is printed on the pieces, which belongs to the form.

## Everything else the site needs

Mark every row build, later or never, and say who decided.

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | | |
| A page for each project | | |
| Every project listed | | |
| How to reach them, and a CV | | |
| What others say | | |
| Languages | | |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | | |
| The page for an address that is not there | | |
| A blog | | |
| A chat | | |
| A legal notice, where their country asks for one | | |

## What you ask for

A yes to the script, or what to change. Give the list of what you decided for them with it.
# Building

## The spine and its look

Build the opening, one middle chapter and the ending in two or three looks.
Let the person scroll those looks, ask which they choose, and stop for their
answer before building the remaining chapters. An unanswered question in
this turn is not a refusal to choose or permission to choose for them.

## The chapters and their words

After the look choice, build the remaining chapters. For the opening and
closing wording, show three versions of each whole beat, including the
surrounding fixed text. Recommend one and leave room for their own wording.
Stop for the choice, then use it word for word.

## The scene

Compare the running scene with the storyboard at its settled beats. Can the visitor inspect the work relationship or evidence the pieces were meant to show, rather than only read its names? Revise the composition when the explanation lives only in the surrounding prose. Keep that accessible prose; it does not replace what the scene was meant to show.

Inspect the changes between beats in both scroll directions, including intermediate positions. When words on the pieces change, correct any overlap that makes the old and new words unreadable together. A readable settled beat does not establish a readable transition.

I’m proposing ten beats across five checklist chapters—shorter than the skill’s usual range because there is one project, no available trace, and no confirmed resolution to the radio problem. The ending will make your lesson explicit: a firmware decision needs a physical observation, and an estimate supports a different claim from an observed run.

/bin/bash -lc "cat > docs/story/storyboard.md <<'EOF'
# Storyboard — Ada Mensah / the bring-up fixture

Status: proposed 21 October 2026; awaiting the user's yes or changes. Concept 1 is selected by the user's explicit delegation. This is the complete script structure and site scope, not final captions, final visual look or approval to publish.

## Story contract

- **Audience:** firmware hiring manager.
- **Question:** How does a firmware decision become something you can check?
- **Form:** bring-up checklist: Prepare → Command → Access → Observe → Record.
- **Object:** one generic bring-up fixture, assembled from seven solid base/contact segments. The same seven segments persist from first screen to last. No sheets, paper, cards, private circuit reconstruction or unrelated effects.
- **Starting meaning:** Ada's stated lesson, that a firmware decision needs a physical observation, gives the assembly its purpose. The fixture's contacts and solid bases gather into a whole; no invented origin story or learning chronology.
- **Closing answer (meaning, not caption):** a firmware decision needs a physical observation; the observation and its scope determine what can be claimed. Mosslink's reported radio-awake observation leaves cause/resolution open. The two-year battery projection is not the 72-hour observed run, six bench-tested samples are not a forty-unit field pilot, and a preliminary emissions check is not completed qualification. F3/F4/F5/F6/F8/F9 establish these distinctions. Contact is the next action after this answer, not the answer itself.
- **Scope exception to approve:** **10 beats, 11.5 screen heights**, instead of the usual 12–22 beats. One confirmed project and no available original measurement artifacts support this shorter story. Do not pad the story with biography, fake plots, extra projects or a resolved-fault narrative. This shorter scope is proposed for the same approval as the storyboard.
- **Attribution:** “Ada” applies only to writing firmware, scheduling states and building the fixture. Assembly/testing/qualification counts are project facts; no implication Ada personally performed them all. The colleague owns PCB and analogue-front-end design.

## Chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | Role | What it tells | What the pieces do | What the visitor can touch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Prepare | Opening / who | Name, embedded-firmware goal, own contribution and physical-observation lesson; scope of responsibility | Seven solid fixture segments gather into one bench assembly; grouped markings separate firmware/fixture contribution from colleague hardware contribution | Ordinary navigation, Mosslink project, view/download CV, email, skip to Record |
| 2 | Command | How | State scheduling; state table, timing diagram and current trace as working documents | The same fixture separates its command side from its observation side.
